english: In a survey of $300$ households of a town about three newspapers $H$, $E$ and $T$, it was found that $150$, $120$ and $85$ households read $H$, $E$ and $T$, respectively; $45$ households read both $H$ and $E$, $30$ read both $E$ and $T$, and $20$ read both $T$ and $H$. The number of households that read none of the three newspapers is equal to the number of households that read all three. Among the households that read at least one of the three newspapers, exactly $p$ percent read exactly two of them. Then the value of $p$ is ______.
hindi: किसी नगर के $300$ परिवारों में तीन समाचार पत्रों $H$, $E$ तथा $T$ के बारे में किए गए एक सर्वेक्षण में पाया गया कि $150$, $120$ तथा $85$ परिवार क्रमशः $H$, $E$ तथा $T$ पढ़ते हैं; $45$ परिवार $H$ तथा $E$ दोनों पढ़ते हैं, $30$ परिवार $E$ तथा $T$ दोनों पढ़ते हैं, और $20$ परिवार $T$ तथा $H$ दोनों पढ़ते हैं। तीनों में से कोई भी समाचार पत्र न पढ़ने वाले परिवारों की संख्या, तीनों समाचार पत्र पढ़ने वाले परिवारों की संख्या के बराबर है। तीनों में से कम से कम एक समाचार पत्र पढ़ने वाले परिवारों में से ठीक $p$ प्रतिशत परिवार उनमें से ठीक दो समाचार पत्र पढ़ते हैं। तब $p$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Let $k=n(H\cap E\cap T)$. Then $n(H\cup E\cup T)=355-95+k=260+k$
Exactly two $=95-3k=35$ (each triple household is counted in all three pairwise numbers)
At least one $=260+20=280$ (all Venn regions are non-negative; $T\cap H$ only $=0$)
solution_full: Let $k$ be the number of households that read all three newspapers, $k=n(H\cap E\cap T)$.
By the formula for three sets, $n(H\cup E\cup T)=355-95+k=260+k$.
The number reading none is $300-n(H\cup E\cup T)=40-k$. This equals $k$, so $40-k=k$, giving $k=20$.
In the Venn diagram, a household in exactly two of the sets is counted once in the pairwise total $95$, and a household in all three is counted three times. So exactly two $=95-3k=95-60=35$.

Check that the data are consistent (every region non-negative): $H\cap E$ only $=25$, $E\cap T$ only $=10$, $T\cap H$ only $=0$; $H$ only $=150-25-0-20=105$, $E$ only $=120-25-10-20=65$, $T$ only $=85-10-0-20=55$; total in at least one $=105+65+55+25+10+0+20=280=260+k$.
So $280$ households read at least one newspaper, and $35$ of them read exactly two.
originality_note: New: the number of households reading all three newspapers is not given but is fixed by the condition 'none = all three', which closes the inclusion-exclusion equation; the answer is a percentage of exactly-two readers among readers (way 5: link between the three-set formula and the exactly-two count). Closest known: survey problems that give every intersection including the triple one, and the GMAT-style 'none equals all three' subscription problems. Different because: the asked ratio is relative to readers only and needs the exactly-two count 95 - 3k after solving for k.
stem_review: Read as a student: every set, the universal set where needed and every symbol is introduced before use, all conditions are stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently in Python (sympy and brute force), is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Checked that the data are consistent (all Venn regions non-negative) and that 'p percent' of the readers is exact (12.5). Used the word 'percent' rather than the percent sign, which the build does not allow outside maths. Changed: wrote 'exactly p percent' and named the base (households reading at least one); no other change.
key_step: Using none = all three in n(H union E union T) = 355 - 95 + k to get k = 20, then exactly two = 95 - 3k.
justification: Routine chain: three-set formula with an unknown triple count, a complement condition, the exactly-two formula and a percentage. No insight beyond standard Venn work; more steps than the single inclusion-exclusion of 2021-P2-Q17 (L1), similar to recovering data from aggregates in 2026-P2-Q12 (L2).
